data.name: Raging Titan
data.detailed_description:
Raging Titan is a tower defense game in which you must defend your headquarters against waves of enemies rushing towards you. Build your towers, plan your efforts, watch out for changing paths and strike back against the alien invaders!
Show your tactical genius, your military leadership and your strategic thinking in this demanding fight!



War has come to Earth! Evil forces are attacking cities all around the world in an effort to extinguish mankind. The best military commanders are needed to fight the threat and save the life on the planet!

You are their archetype. A tactical genius, a fighter without fear. Equipped with a sense for the situation and experience of years of battle. You are sent as the spearhead to stop the enemies. It is in your hands whether we will survive or be forgotten!


Plan your best strategy and prevent your enemies from reaching their goal by building your defense towers. Control the enemy paths, shape the path they take to attack your and destroy them with a selection of your weapons!




Select the best from a selection of 10 hugely different towers. Control the masses by forcing them down a certain path with your Machine Gun towers, use the Plasma or Rocket towers as the backbone of your defense, or fry your enemies with a deadly lighting strike. Find the best tower for the types of enemies you are expecting and upgrade them in 3 different stages!




Shields, armor, airborne, walking, big and small - there are many enemies and each of them require a special tactic and counter measure to defeat them. Battle the robot infantry and face their bosses until the final command raider takes the battle into its own claws to bring down your Command HQ!




From fertile grasslands to the desert, from volcanic fissure to abandoned cities and from frozen mountain peaks to once beautiful beaches - fight the battle in 25 levels and diverse landscapes!

reviews.review:
Raging Titan is a science fiction tower defense game that combines strategic construction, battlefield management, and tactical decision-making into a straightforward but engaging experience. Developed and published by Mad Vulture Games, the game places players in command of Earth's resistance against an overwhelming alien invasion. With hostile mechanical forces threatening humanity's survival, the objective is to establish effective defensive positions and prevent enemies from reaching the command headquarters. Rather than depending on complicated storytelling or elaborate gameplay systems, it concentrates on the fundamental appeal of tower defense: planning ahead, managing resources, and adapting to increasingly dangerous enemy formations. Its most interesting feature is the ability to influence enemy movement through defensive construction, adding a welcome element of creativity to an otherwise familiar strategic formula.

The gameplay centers on building and upgrading defensive towers while surviving successive waves of attackers. Players must carefully evaluate the battlefield, determine where enemies are likely to travel, and construct defenses capable of eliminating them before they reach their destination. Unlike tower defense games that rely entirely on fixed enemy routes, Raging Titan allows players to manipulate movement patterns through strategic tower placement. This creates opportunities to establish lengthy defensive corridors, concentrate enemy forces into vulnerable positions, and maximize the effectiveness of available weapons. The mechanic encourages experimentation because the placement of a single structure can influence the overall defensive arrangement. Success therefore depends not only on offensive strength but also on understanding how enemies navigate the environment.

One of the game's strongest features is its selection of ten defensive tower types, each contributing different tactical possibilities. Machine Gun towers can help direct enemy movement, while Plasma and Rocket towers provide substantial offensive capabilities. Lightning-based defenses introduce another method of dealing with approaching threats. Every tower can be improved through three upgrade stages, allowing players to strengthen their existing positions as encounters become more demanding. Choosing between upgrading established structures and constructing additional defenses creates an important strategic consideration. A powerful concentration of weapons may be effective against certain opponents, but broader battlefield coverage can become essential when enemies approach through complicated routes. Although the system offers meaningful variety, its relatively conventional progression may feel limited to players accustomed to more elaborate tower defense mechanics.

Enemy diversity contributes significantly to the challenge. The invading forces include mechanical infantry, heavily armored opponents, shielded enemies, airborne attackers, and larger adversaries requiring specialized responses. These differences encourage players to reconsider their defensive priorities instead of relying on a single strategy throughout the campaign. A formation capable of destroying ordinary ground units may struggle against more durable or mobile enemies, making adaptability essential. Boss encounters provide additional challenges, culminating in a confrontation with a formidable command raider threatening the headquarters. While the enemy designs follow recognizable science fiction conventions, their varied defensive characteristics create opportunities for tactical problem-solving and reinforce the importance of selecting appropriate weapons.

The campaign contains 25 levels distributed across several environments, including grassy landscapes, deserts, volcanic terrain, abandoned urban areas, frozen mountains, and coastal locations. This geographical variety gives the invasion a broader sense of scale while preventing the visual presentation from becoming entirely repetitive. Each battlefield offers another opportunity to reconsider defensive positioning and experiment with different approaches. The environments support the game's military science fiction atmosphere, although their visual presentation remains relatively modest. The colorful landscapes, mechanical enemies, and futuristic weapons establish a recognizable aesthetic without attempting the graphical sophistication of larger productions. The presentation is serviceable and generally consistent with the game's independent development scope, but players expecting highly detailed environments or elaborate visual effects may find it somewhat basic.

The experience also benefits from its accessible premise and uncomplicated structure. Understanding the objective requires little explanation, making it approachable for newcomers while still offering tactical considerations for experienced players. However, the simplicity of its design can also become a weakness. Much of the entertainment depends on repeated cycles of constructing defenses, eliminating enemies, and refining strategies. Players who enjoy optimizing tower placement will likely appreciate this repetition, whereas those seeking extensive narrative development, unusual mission objectives, or complex progression systems may eventually find the experience predictable. The effectiveness of its challenge largely rests on whether different enemy combinations and battlefield layouts continue to encourage meaningful adjustments.

Additional features include Steam achievements, leaderboards, and a single-player campaign, providing some motivation for players interested in completing objectives or improving their performance. A downloadable demo also offers an opportunity to become familiar with the mechanics before purchasing the full experience. Its modest computer requirements make it relatively approachable for players using less powerful hardware. Regarding Steam Deck compatibility, Raging Titan currently has an Unknown or unverified status, with no official Valve confirmation that it meets the requirements for Verified or Playable classification. Although its modest technical demands are encouraging, compatibility with Proton, controller functionality, and interface readability cannot be guaranteed. Players interested in handheld gameplay should therefore be prepared for possible control adjustments or compatibility limitations.

Ultimately, Raging Titan is a respectable independent tower defense game whose greatest attraction is the freedom to shape enemy routes while constructing increasingly powerful defensive networks. Its combination of ten tower types, multiple upgrades, diverse enemies, and 25 campaign levels provides a reasonable amount of strategic content. The relatively simple presentation, conventional progression, and repetitive gameplay structure prevent it from becoming an exceptional genre entry, but its tactical mechanics offer enough substance to entertain players who enjoy defensive planning and battlefield optimization. It is particularly suitable for enthusiasts who appreciate straightforward strategy games with an emphasis on positioning rather than elaborate storytelling. Despite its limitations, the experience demonstrates an interesting understanding of what makes tower defense satisfying.

A solid and accessible tower defense experience featuring creative pathway manipulation, varied defensive options, and enjoyable tactical challenges, although its modest production values and limited mechanical complexity restrict its broader appeal.

Rating: 7/10
